toolbar.reducedHint: Your system asks for reduced motion: nothing moves, the arrows show the direction.

legend.doc: everything without a badge shows what the registry documents. A linked item without data says “No data” – never OK.
legend.flowMoving: Documented flow – the moving dashes show its direction
legend.flowStatic: Documented flow – the arrow shows its direction
legend.numbersPoints: Data points that take the way

fromAny.monitor: From the monitors linked to it

live.hiddenSource: A check you may not see
live.hiddenWord: A check you may not see: {{word}}
live.fromHidden: From a check you may not see: it counts towards the status, without its name or details.

graph.label: Picture: {{title}}
graph.nodeHelp: Tab moves to the next part, Enter opens its page.
graph.edgeHelp: A way of the documented flow.
graph.partial: Drag to see the rest; the buttons zoom.

path.help: Point at an entry to see its way; a click keeps it highlighted.

flow.title: Data flow
flow.help: Where the data of this {{type}} goes, as the registry documents it: interfaces, the gateway that collects them, where they are published, the KPI jobs that read them and where their results are shown.
flow.live: monitors linked to the asset, the freshness of the datasets its KPI jobs write, and the plant checks.
flow.emptyText: Assign a device profile to see the data flow: on the overview, under Data and KPIs, choose the profile and set up its interfaces.
flow.whoCanAct: Whoever manages the site assigns device profiles.
flow.noProfile: No device profile is assigned: only the KPI jobs are drawn.

lineage.title: Lineage
lineage.help: Which {{type}} deliver this data point, where each publishes it and which KPIs read it.
lineage.live: monitors linked to an asset, the freshness of the datasets of the KPI jobs, and the plant checks.
lineage.grouped: Many {{type}} have this profile: the picture shows one node per {{site}}; the table lists every one.
lineage.emptyText: Assign the device profile to an {{type}} to see where this data point goes.

structure.title: Structure
structure.help: The site’s hierarchy after ISA-95, each part sized by its {{type}}. A click opens a part; the path above goes back.
structure.live: the inner ring and the counts show monitors linked to assets. The outer ring is the documented status of the assets.
structure.more: {{count}} more – the assets list shows all of them.
structure.truncated: This site has more assets than the picture lists – the assets list shows all of them.
structure.emptyText: Add {{areas}}, work centers and work units, and place {{assets}} in them, to see the structure.
structure.ringLegend: Ring: assets by status; inner ring: linked monitors

coverage.title: KPI coverage
coverage.help: Which {{type}} have a KPI, could have it (they deliver every input) or cannot (inputs missing) – and where a check fails.
coverage.live: the plant checks (a problem). Has, could and cannot follow from what the registry documents.

legend.has: Has it: a KPI job is set up
legend.problem: Problem: a plant check of the job fails
legend.could: Could have it: delivers every input, no job yet
legend.ready: Collected – ready: the device delivers every input and a data collection maps each of them, no job yet
legend.collect: Device delivers, not collected: every input is delivered, but no data collection maps all of them yet
legend.cannot: Cannot: inputs are missing (the cell says which)
legend.unchecked: Not checked: the KPI reads no data points

coverage.pctHelp: Jobs set up, of all the KPIs the assets could have
coverage.couldHint: Add a KPI job on the asset page (Data and KPIs).
coverage.collectHint: Map the inputs in a data collection of the asset (Data collections), then add a KPI job.
coverage.potential: KPI potential: {{ready}} ready, {{collect}} need a data collection
coverage.byPlace: KPI potential by site and area
coverage.truncated: {{shown}} of {{total}} listed – narrow the filters to see the rest. The counts above cover all of them.
coverage.noKpisText: Add KPI definitions (Plant → KPI definitions) to see which assets have them.
coverage.noAssetsText: Add {{type}} to a site to see their KPI coverage.
coverage.cannotWith: {{type}} with a profile that cannot have it

tiles.coverageHint: KPI jobs set up, of all the KPIs the site’s assets could have (they deliver every input).
tiles.title: Overview

info.hint: Point at an asset, a VLAN or a zone to see its devices, subnets and VLANs.

network.title: Diagram
network.help: Zones (IEC 62443-3-2) in bands by their level, field at the bottom, with their VLANs and {{type}}; conduits are the gates between them. Point at a part or select it for its details.
network.live: the checks linked to an asset and its devices (monitors – Gatus, CheckMk, the MQTT silent-device and Kafka checks – and dataset freshness): online, offline, or “no data”. A way from an offline asset is red and still.
network.emptyText: Add zones and VLANs, and devices and data paths of the {{type}}, to see the diagram.
network.notDrawn_one: {{count}} {{type}} without devices or data paths is not drawn.
network.notDrawn_other: {{count}} {{type}} without devices or data paths are not drawn.
network.legendVlan: VLAN (IEEE 802.1Q) in a zone, the assets on it
network.legendConduit: Conduit: the gate between two zones; data paths into another zone run through it
network.legendNoConduit: A data path into another zone without a documented conduit
network.legendOnline: From an asset its checks say is online
network.legendOffline: From an asset its checks say is offline
network.nodeHelp: Tab moves to the next part. Space selects it, Enter opens its page, Escape clears the selection.
network.search: Find a part or data path
network.searchPlaceholder: Find an asset, host, data path …
network.filterNoConduit: Only paths without a documented conduit
network.legendLevels: Bands: the levels of the Purdue model, field at the bottom, the enterprise network and cloud at the top – data paths run upwards
network.legendLabels: Protocols and ports of a way: point at it, or select a part or data path
network.clearSelectionHint: Or press Escape, or click an empty spot
network.pathsHelp: Point at an entry to see its way; a click selects it.
